subject: Tenor hybridization: proposed 18-month uplift with sprint tokens & cohort harmonization
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@astrahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: 18-month hybrid term + sprint tokens — proposal for harmonizing subsidiaries

Hi Aisha,

Thanks for the call this morning — really appreciate the clarity on AstraHealth's Q4 expansion timelines. Per our conversation, I attached a first-pass amendment that aims to: (1) align the three product subsidiaries on a single co-term date, (2) provide a graduated 18-month commitment (12 months annualized + a 6-month flexible sprint allocation), and (3) introduce an operational buffer for burst capacity we call "sprint tokens."

High level summary in the attachment (Redwood_Amendment_v2.pdf):
- Term: 18 months total, effective 2026-10-01 -> 2028-03-31. Billing will be annualized (first 12 months billed up front) with a final 6-month ramp window.
- Sprint tokens: a pool of 100k token-equivalents that can be used for short-term bursts; unused tokens after the 6-month window convert to a 30% credit toward the next renewals pool.
- Co-terming: subsidiaries (AstraHealth Core, AstraHealth Insights, AstraHealth Telecare) will be aligned to the 2028-03-31 term boundary via staged top-ups over the first 9 months.
- Early-exit / true-up: a limited escape hatch for org restructure (90-day notice + 25% unwind fee).
- Pricing: blended unit price anchored to committed volume with a 12% uplift on overages; detailed bands are in the spreadsheet (Sprint-Tokens-Calculator.xlsx).

Next steps I recommend:
1) You review the PDF and the token calculator; flag any carve-outs for Telecare.
2) If acceptable, we’ll route the amendment through legal and finance and prepare a DocuSign for signature.
3) We can schedule a short canary window (2 weeks) after effective date for the Telecare cutover.

I left margin notes in the PDF where we discussed special billing treatment for grants. If you're ok, I'll loop in our finance lead (Kimberly) to confirm the annualization mechanics and provide an invoice preview.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: Redwood_Amendment_v2.pdf (pdf), Sprint-Tokens-Calculator.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Aisha Raman <aisha.raman@astrahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Jacobs <ben.jacobs@astrahealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Sep 2026 12:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Draft: 18-month hybrid term + sprint tokens — proposal for harmonizing subsidiaries

Marissa,

Thanks for the quick turnaround; reviewed the PDF and spreadsheet this afternoon. Overall this structure could work — a few asks from procurement and finance before we can move to signatures:

1) Can the sprint tokens be split across subsidiaries instead of a single pool? Telecare needs a guaranteed 25k minimum.
2) The annualized billing approach is a bit heavy for our grants budget. Can we shift to 6-month invoicing for the first 12 months (still contractually annualized but invoiced in two equal installments)?
3) Need clarity on the 30% conversion of unused tokens — is that capped? We sometimes run multi-week experiments that could leave large residuals.

If you can propose language for (1)-(3) we'll send to our legal and finance for a last review. If it's straightforward we can aim to sign by EOD Friday (our target).

Regards,

Aisha Raman
Sr. Director, Digital Platform Partnerships | AstraHealth
aisha.raman@astrahealth.com

Marissa / Karthik — quick answers so we can close this week: 

1) Per-subsidiary token buckets: operationally feasible. We'll model an API-side quota split and map each subsidiary to a dedicated token sub-pool. Telecare 25k guaranteed is fine; remaining 75k can be shared with a soft-priority routing. There will be a small provisioning overhead (~3% buffer) baked into the token price.

2) Invoicing cadence: We can support 6-month invoicing for the first 12 months (invoice 1 = months 1-6; invoice 2 = months 7-12) while keeping the contractual annualization. Finance will treat the full committed 12-month amount as revenue to be recognized monthly per ASC guidance; the invoicing cadence is a customer convenience only and does not change revenue recognition. I'll include an invoice preview with amounts once Marissa confirms final quantities.

3) Unused token conversion cap: Recommend capping the conversion credit at 50k token-equivalent per renewal cycle to avoid large residual credits being carried forward. The 30% conversion rate stands. If Astra wants a higher cap we can negotiate an increased cap with a slightly lower conversion rate.

Once you confirm I’ll ask Legal to draft the language for the amendment and we can generate a DocuSign packet.

Kimberly Park
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
